item.title: From Idea to MVP in Hours: How AI Made Innovation Accessible for Our Routine
item.dc:creator: Alisson Prata
item.description: In the financial market — and in any high-performance sector — the speed with which we test an idea defines our success.
item.content:encoded:
In the financial market — and in any high-performance sector — the speed with which we test an idea defines our success.

Often, we have valuable insights to improve team productivity, customer service, or data analysis, but these ideas end up shelved. Why? The complexity of taking them off paper.

We've always looked at technology as something that demands long development timelines. But Generative Artificial Intelligence changed this rule of the game.

Today, AI acts as an efficiency lever, allowing business professionals (like you and me) to create their own MVPs (Minimum Viable Products). We can test concepts in practice, validate whether they work, and bring innovation to the table in a simple and dynamic way.

💡 The Practical Case: A Pocket "Mentor"

To illustrate this ease, I want to share a recent experience. I felt the lack of a tool that would help my team quickly consult the principles of the great market masters (Graham, Bogle, Kahneman) in their day-to-day work.

Instead of just wishing for it, I used Google Gemini as my execution partner. The result was Advisor Brain AI, a simple application that analyzes audio and cross-references objections with a library of 50 reference books.

Anyone who wants to test this MVP, the link is open here: 👉 https://advisor-brain-ai.streamlit.app/

But the most interesting part isn't the app itself, but how it was made. The process was incredibly smooth and accessible:

  1. Defining the Problem (The Human): I designed the business logic. What do I need? For the system to listen to an audio, identify the behavioral bias, and suggest a technical and empathetic response.

  2. The Translation (The AI): I didn't need to write the code line by line. I described how it should work to the AI, and it structured the programming language (Python) needed for it to run.

  3. The Refinement (The Collaboration): I asked for adjustments like asking a colleague: "Include this list of books", "Improve the interface", "Add audio support".

  4. The Test (The Deploy): Within a few hours, the idea went from a notepad to a link accessible on a phone, ready to be tested in the field.

Why is this transformative?

This doesn't replace big IT projects. On the contrary, it gives us the power to approach the technical area with more mature, already validated ideas.

This brings productivity. We spend less time imagining "what if..." and more time testing real solutions. The barrier to entry for innovation has dropped drastically. Today, creativity and knowledge of your niche are worth as much as technical capability.

Whether you're a Director seeking efficiency or a Junior wanting to show value: the tools are on the table.

Technology, when well used, is the greatest ally we have to simplify the complex.

What idea would you take off paper today if you knew it was simpler than it seems?

item.title: The New Market Frontier: I Launched an Asset on Ethereum Using Only AI and Strategy
item.dc:creator: Alisson Prata
item.description: The technical barrier between a financial idea and its global execution just collapsed.
item.content:encoded:
The technical barrier between a financial idea and its global execution just collapsed.

I work in the financial market and I'm familiar with programming logic, but for this experiment, I decided to retire my coding skills. The challenge was clear: create, validate, and launch a token operable on the Ethereum network, the most robust infrastructure in the crypto world, using only Artificial Intelligence as a technical partner.

The result wasn't just a functional smart contract, but a practical lesson on the future of our economy.

The Journey: From Prompt to Market

It all started with a conversation with Gemini. Instead of opening a code editor and typing complex lines in Solidity, I described what I wanted: a standard ERC-20 token, with fixed supply and security parameters. The AI not only generated the code but guided me through the deployment process.

The experience was surprisingly smooth. I used Remix, a kind of cloud-based development environment, where I simply "pasted" the logic generated by the AI. With a few clicks and a fee paid in ETH via MetaMask, the contract was live on the blockchain.

But a digital asset needs credibility. The next step was to register the contract on Etherscan. It's the digital equivalent of going to a notary office: I made the code public and auditable. Without writing a single line of code, I had a verified, transparent asset. 👉 You can check the verified contract here: https://etherscan.io/address/0xd48be668b8ce75cf3a035dc866f3fb215a9ee819

The final step was market creation. On Uniswap, the world's largest decentralized exchange, I created a "liquidity pool." I deposited an amount of ETH against my new token, and the asset instantly gained a price. What would take months of structuring in traditional markets (IPO, bookbuilding) was resolved in minutes. 👉 See the active trading on Uniswap: https://app.uniswap.org/explore/tokens/ethereum/0xd48be668b8ce75cf3a035dc866f3fb215a9ee819 👉 Or follow the chart on DexScreener: https://dexscreener.com/ethereum/0xbfab12083ce00afec8ef1c71638c8c198720eef6725cb869eb89b6859a53548b

The Real Economy Revolution

Watching the token being traded and showing up on market monitors, it clicks. This isn't just about speculative cryptocurrencies. The infrastructure I used for this test is the same one that, very soon, will support the real economy.

Picture this same process applied to debentures, real estate fund shares, or CRIs. Ethereum technology enables instant settlement (T+0), absolute transparency, and fractionalization of global assets. The operational complexity that today costs banks billions has been reduced to a smart contract that an AI can help write.

The Paradox of Ease: The Invisible Risk

However, the experience brought a red flag. The same simplicity that allowed me, as a legitimate professional, to create a legitimate project, hands terrifying firepower to scammers.

There's no ethical filter in the code. During the process, I noticed the "unknown token" warnings on the trading interfaces. That's the only initial barrier. Today, creating a fraudulent token to raise funds and disappear (the infamous rug pull) is technically just as easy as creating a legitimate one.

This shifts the responsibility to the end user. In the traditional market, we trust CVM or ANBIMA to filter assets. In the tokenized economy, due diligence is decentralized. Fundamental analysis and contract auditing become mandatory survival skills.

Conclusion

My experiment proved that technology is no longer the bottleneck. AI has democratized access to the financial market's "machine." The competitive edge is no longer "who knows how to code" but "who has the best thesis and the best ethics."

The future of finance will be hybrid: built by artificial intelligence, but, more than ever, dependent on human integrity.

item.title: Market Outlook for 2025: What Leading Fund Managers Are Seeing
item.dc:creator: Alisson Prata
item.description: Brazil's leading fund managers begin 2025 with a predominantly cautious tone, reflecting the macroeconomic and political uncertainties dominating the global landscape. Based on…
item.content:encoded:
Brazil's leading fund managers begin 2025 with a predominantly cautious tone, reflecting the macroeconomic and political uncertainties dominating the global landscape. Based on a detailed analysis of letters from 15 asset managers, using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, it was possible to consolidate the main market perceptions and identify the central themes that should guide investment decisions throughout the year.

The overall sentiment captured in the analysis shows a neutral to slightly negative bias, with managers closely monitoring factors such as global monetary policy, inflation, and fiscal instability in Brazil. Most letters maintain a wait-and-see tone, awaiting greater clarity before adopting more aggressive positioning. Some show a more pronounced pessimism, warning of the risks of persistent inflation, currency volatility, and the conduct of domestic fiscal policy. A smaller, though still minority, group sees opportunities in specific sectors, mainly in the Brazilian stock market and commodities.

The main focus of the analyses remains the trajectory of global monetary policy, with emphasis on the Federal Reserve (FED), which keeps interest rates elevated and puts pressure on emerging markets. The European Central Bank (ECB) and the Bank of Japan, on the other hand, signal easing cycles, creating an environment of divergence among major economies. This misalignment of monetary policies can generate volatility in financial markets, something managers are watching closely.

In Brazil, inflation remains a central challenge, especially in services core inflation, driven by a still-tight labor market and rising wages. The Brazilian Central Bank raised the interest rate again in an attempt to contain this movement, but inflation expectations remain unanchored relative to the target.

Fiscal policy is also a recurring concern. Managers point out that the government maintains an expansionary stance, which could put further pressure on inflation and compromise the trajectory toward fiscal balance. The market is already beginning to price in the impacts of the 2026 elections and the effect of changes in the political landscape on economic policy in the coming years. The growing influence of religious groups in national politics appears as one of the factors that could alter the direction of the government and of structural reforms.

In the stock market, the Ibovespa rose 4.9% in January, driven mainly by the banking and construction sectors. However, some sectors are facing difficulties, such as car rental and proteins, impacted by the exchange rate and tighter credit. In the commodities market, gold and corn stood out positively, while oil posted a moderate gain, though with significant volatility. The real remains weak against the dollar, benefiting exporters but putting pressure on importers and sectors dependent on foreign inputs.

From a strategic standpoint, managers have adopted a mostly defensive positioning. Exposure to inflation-linked assets, such as gold and agricultural commodities, stands out as one of the main choices, while the dollar continues to be used as a hedge against currency swings. Allocation to equities remains selective, focused on sectors considered more resilient, such as energy and infrastructure. There is also a move toward preserving liquidity, awaiting clearer signals about the direction of the economy before increasing risk exposure.

The start of 2025 reinforces a scenario of uncertainty, demanding a high level of monitoring and adaptation from managers. The trajectory of global monetary policy, the unfolding of inflation in Brazil, and the first signs of the 2026 election race should be the main drivers of risk and opportunity for markets in the coming months. Caution remains the main guideline for strategies, as investors seek a balance between protection and tactical positioning amid market swings.

item.title: Why Should We Teach Children to Code?
item.dc:creator: Alisson Prata
item.description: In recent years, influential people around the world, such as Bill Gates, Mark Zuckerberg, and even American president Barack Obama, have spoken out about the importance of teaching programming to…
item.content:encoded:
In recent years, influential people around the world, such as Bill Gates, Mark Zuckerberg, and even American president Barack Obama, have spoken out about the importance of teaching programming to our children. Several institutions focused on this goal are emerging, such as Code Club and Code. Some countries, such as the United States and England, are already including this subject in their curricula. But after all, why is it so important to teach programming to children?

Watch the video

We live in a world dominated by software. Our phones, TVs, and even our refrigerators are already connected to the internet. We can already buy almost everything online, and does anyone remember the last time they bought a map? People no longer buy encyclopedias, after all, it's all on Google. Soon our homes will be controlled by software. Virtual money is already a reality, and we all already know there are cars that don't need drivers.

Demand for information technology professionals keeps increasing, since most everyday objects are no longer merely electrical/mechanical objects and are becoming digital. Many professions based on repetitive processes and simple decisions are being replaced by equipment capable of performing such tasks with greater precision and lower cost than humans. This does not mean that machines will take over the world (not yet), but it does mean that professions are changing, and it is our duty to prepare children for these changes.

In the future, learning computational logic will be as important as reading, writing, and doing math operations. This does not mean that everyone will be a software engineer in the future, or that all professionals will use these skills in their jobs. What matters, however, is learning computational logic, giving individuals the ability to solve problems by combining logic, math, and algorithms.

Computational logic teaches us to break big problems down into smaller, more manageable problems. We can use this way of thinking to model real-world problems, separating out the most relevant aspects so we can solve problems more efficiently, on a smaller scale, and ensure that the solutions to these problems are representative of the real world.

The goals of teaching programming to children go beyond simply preparing them for the job market. Different fields of study, such as engineering, physics, biology, and music, can benefit from the use of computational logic. It is present, for example, in the business world, where large companies need to analyze extremely complex market data and turn it into useful information that will support the company's strategic decision-making processes.

The Third Industrial Revolution is already underway, and we need to be prepared for major changes. The best way to help ensure everyone is prepared may be through education, so it is up to all of us to encourage and promote the teaching of technology to children and young people around the world. We don't have to be mere spectators of technology; we can be its creators.
